- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggesting lag in adjusting to actual market momentum.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate gradual decline after sharp spikes.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the second half of the forecast (days 15–30), often overcorrecting after initial spikes.
- Forecast does not account for recent price volatility; tends to smooth out sharp moves, leading to underestimation of true volatility.
- Model reacts too slowly to new data; true outcomes often exceed forecasts by 1–2% in the first 5 days, then converge later.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model peaks too high and then falls too fast, missing the true peak or trough.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently 1–3% higher than true outcomes, especially in the middle to end of the horizon.
